A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HyperClus-G study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original clustering experiments on nine UCI-derived datasets, including NCut, F1, runtime, eigenvalue comparisons, and EDVW ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix C. Results retained from v1 still qualify as original empirical results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same transition matrix, stationary distribution computation, normalized Laplacian, second eigenvector, and sign-based partitioning. The recursive strategies for k-way clustering are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine UCI-derived hypergraphs, with the same two-way and k-way clustering tasks and constant-weight EIVW ablation scenario. Dataset descriptions and coverage are retained in v2 Appendix C.2.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain STAR++, CLIQUE++, DiffEq, node2vec, and event2vec/hyperedge2vec, with actual-label partitions additionally compared for NCut. Comparator membership in the ablation and runtime tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: Dataset subsets, feature quantization, label-derived EDVW assignments, NCut and F1 evaluation, recursive clustering procedures, and baseline configurations are retained. The additional k-way NCut definition in v2 Appendix C.4 restates the existing metric rather than changing the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The eigenvalue-versus-NCut analysis and all-one-EDVW ablation in v1 Sections 6.3–6.4 remain in v2 Sections 5.3–5.4 with the same evidence. No additional empirical robustness, sensitivity, or error analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten runs for nondeterministic baselines, their means, and appendix standard deviations for node2vec and hyperedge2vec. The reporting practice and corresponding uncertainty tables are unchanged.

E6.justification: All matched numerical tables are unchanged: v1 Tables 3–12 correspond to v2 Tables 4–13. This includes benchmark scores, eigenvalue approximation errors, ablation results, runtimes, and standard deviations; for example, HyperClus-G's Mushroom NCut remains 0.6388 and Rice's approximation error remains 24.91%.

T1.justification: v1 Section 4.2 uses NCut(returned) approximately equal to the eigenvalue to argue linear optimality. v2 adds a lower-bound observation and asserts that no general O(eigenvalue) upper bound holds for sign-threshold cuts, naming a dumbbell-graph counterexample without deriving it. This substantially qualifies the central theoretical argument, although Theorem 2 remains unchanged. Appendices A.6–A.7 also contain limited algebraic corrections.

C1.justification: Section 1.1 narrows the novelty claim from the first work on hypergraph Rayleigh quotients to the first for EDVW hypergraphs, acknowledging earlier EIVW work. The principal algorithm, Cheeger inequality, and asserted approximate linear-optimality contributions remain.

C2.justification: The new qualification in v2 Section 4.2 materially limits interpreting eigenvalue approximation as a general guarantee for the returned partition, but is not reconciled with the retained headline optimality claim. Appendix C.4 additionally identifies direct k-way spectral analysis as an unresolved extension outside the paper's scope.

D1.justification: v2's abstract supplies a HyperClus-G repository address and states that code is available; v1 only refers readers to a README for its own implementation. Hardware, Python version, dependencies, preprocessing, and baseline implementation details are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v1 Section 1.2 is removed, including substantive positioning against Hayashi et al., edge-colored clustering, and Zhu–Segarra EDVW clustering work; the corresponding references are also removed. v2 adds Jost and Mulas, Mulas et al., and Ghojogh et al., narrows Rayleigh-quotient novelty, and emphasizes comparison with Chitra and Raphael through new Table 2.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the narrative: four proof blocks move to Appendices A.6–A.9, complexity analysis moves from Section 5 to Appendix B, experimental appendices become Appendix C, and the related-work subsection disappears. Introductory prose, theorem labeling, citations, and author information are also revised.

P2.justification: v2 adds the spectral-properties comparison in Table 2 and the logical-dependency diagram in Figure 2. It also shrinks and wraps Figure 1 beside text, merges Table 1's weight rows, and reformats the document and retained tables into the TMLR layout.

improvement.justification: The new overview displays, narrower novelty claim, code-access information, and explicit theoretical qualification improve accessibility and transparency. However, v2 removes substantive discussion of closely related EDVW clustering research, while its new Section 4.2 qualification leaves the abstract and Theorem 2's optimality claim unresolved. These material benefits and losses prevent a reliable net judgment of overall improvement.
